resale_co.name: Certificate of Continued Occupancy (CCO)
resale_co.issued_by: Office of Code Enforcement / Construction and Code Enforcement
resale_co.lead_time: Apply at least 10 working days before settlement or occupancy
resale_co.valid_for: Application expires 90 days after inspection if the CCO has not been issued
requirements: House number visible from the street, at least 4 inches tall
Steps free of cracks and trip hazards, even treads and risers, closed risers (4 inch ball rule)
Sidewalks, aprons and driveways level with no cracks or lifts over 1/2 inch; driveway parking surface must be impervious (no stone or gravel)
Graspable handrail on steps with 4 or more risers; guardrails where porch, landing or stairs are over 30 inches above grade
Property free of debris and hazards; abandoned tanks and wells removed with a permit
No peeling paint or rust on exterior surfaces
Gutters and downspouts secure and clear, with splash blocks or diverters
Foundation openings sealed; basement and crawlspace windows intact; Bilco doors and crawlspace access working and sealed
Exterior receptacles, including garages and sheds, GFCI protected
Window glass intact; electric service cable secured; damaged wiring and fixtures replaced
Approved chimney cap
Zoning and construction permits for additions, pools, sheds, garages, decks and fences; open permits must be closed
Swimming pool: bonding/grounding certificate from a licensed NJ electrician dated within 30 days of the application, plus pool affidavit

fees.label: Residential dwelling CCO application
fees.quote: Certificate of Continued Occupancy Application Residential Dwelling Fee: $100.00 $25.00 Fee after first reinspection

fees.label: Commercial / Multi Family CCO application (may apply to a 2-family sale; not confirmed)
fees.quote: Certificate of Continued Occupancy Application Commercial/Multi Family Fee: $150.00 $25.00 Fee after first reinspection

resale_co.how_to_apply: Download the Residential CCO application (3 pages, including a swimming pool affidavit), complete it, and submit it with a check to the Office of Code Enforcement, 24 N. Black Horse Pike, Runnemede, NJ 08078. Call 856-939-2815 with questions.

evidence.quote: EXTERIOR COMPLIANCE REQUIREMENTS Certificate of Continued Occupancy for the sale of a single-family dwelling. FORM ISSUE DATE, 07/17/2020

Application must be submitted at least 10 Working days prior to settlement or occupancy date. All work must be completed before a Certificate can be issued. Application expires 90 days after inspection, if the Certificate of Continued Occupancy has not been issued
Please note that you must close out any open construction permits before selling your home. Contact the construction office at 856-939-2815.

resale_co.notes: The residential CCO application has a 'Buyer/Sale' or 'Rental/Tenant' checkbox, and the borough publishes an exterior-only compliance list for the sale of a single-family dwelling. A separate interior and exterior list applies to rentals, commercial, and multi-family sales, so a 2-family sale may fall under the Commercial/Multi Family form ($150) and the fuller interior list; this was not confirmed. The municipal code (ecode360 RU0329) could not be opened, so the ordinance text requiring the CCO on sale was not read directly. Code Enforcement: 856-939-5161 x1006. Construction Official: Keith Raveling.

requirements: Smoke alarm requirements depend on the year the home was built (pre-1977 battery alarms on each level; later eras need 120V hardwired, interconnected alarms as listed in the borough table)
Where no alarms exist or battery alarms are being replaced, use 10-year sealed battery alarms; hardwired alarms cannot be replaced with battery alarms
Smoke alarms must not be over 10 years old from date of manufacture
Alarms must be mounted with proper hardware; nails, thumbtacks, tape or Velcro are not acceptable
Carbon monoxide alarm in the hall outside bedrooms, no more than 10 feet from any bedroom
Monitored alarm systems in homes built 1977 or later must be maintained at change of occupancy
Secondary power source label ('CAUTION: MULTIPLE SOURCES OF POWER') within 18 inches of the main panel and meter if the home has a generator, solar panels or battery storage
The borough states that since February 2025 a fire extinguisher is no longer required for the certificate

authorities.how_to_apply: Request a Smoke Detector & Carbon Monoxide Alarm inspection through the borough's SDL online portal (linked from the Fire Prevention / Inspections page). The March 2025 paper application said fees are payable to the Borough of Runnemede by check or money order, no refunds.

evidence.quote: To apply for a Smoke Detector & Carbon Monoxide Alarm inspection, scan the code below: Or visit www.runnemedenj.org/public-safety/fire-prevention

As of February 2025, due to a change in the New Jersey Uniform Fire Code, a fire extinguisher is no longer required in residential properties when obtaining a Certificate of Smoke and Carbon Monoxide Alarm for a change of ownership or tenancy.
Fees Payable to: Borough of Runnemede (Check or Money Order) NO REFUNDS

fire_cert.notes: Fees come from the borough's March 2025 application PDF, which is no longer on the live site (the old runnemedenj.org/wp-content URL now returns 404); it was read from the Internet Archive copy captured 2025-08-03. The live 'Smoke Detector & Carbon Monoxide Alarm Inspection Requests' link now redirects to the SDL portal (https://www.sdlportal.com/towns/nj/camden/runnemede/requests/smokeAlarm), which requires a citizen login, so current fees could not be re-confirmed. Fire Prevention page lists (856) 939-5161; the fire marshal documents list 856-939-2817 (Captain / Fire Official Michael Kearney). The borough's claim that extinguishers are no longer required since February 2025 differs from the brief's state baseline and should be checked against the current N.J.A.C. 5:70.

other_items.label: Open construction permits must be closed before sale
other_items.detail: Any permits without final inspection or certificate of approval must be closed out before the CCO is issued; permits are required for any work done without permits.

other_items.label: Swimming pool affidavit and bonding certificate
other_items.detail: Pool affidavit is page 3 of the residential CCO application; a bonding/grounding certificate from a licensed NJ electrician dated within 30 days is required if there is a pool.

open_questions: Which CCO form and fee applies to a 2-family (duplex) sale: Residential ($100) or Commercial/Multi Family ($150)?
Whether the single-family sale inspection is exterior-only (as the published list suggests) or also interior.
Current fire certificate fees in the SDL portal (last confirmed fees are from the March 2025 paper application).
